evals.name: espresso
evals.prompt: Using lcaac, model the carbon footprint of one cup of espresso: 7 g of ground coffee at 5 kg CO2-eq per kg, 0.05 kWh of electricity from the French grid at 0.05 kg CO2-eq per kWh, and 50 ml of tap water whose impacts we ignore. Call the main process espresso, and add a test.
evals.expected_output: An .lca model with a process espresso whose climate impact is 0.0375 kg CO2-eq per cup (0.035 from coffee, 0.0025 from electricity), and a passing test.

assertions.text: The tests of the model pass
One cup of espresso emits 0.0375 kg CO2-eq
The climate impact is in the prelude's unit kg_CO2_Eq, not in a unit declared by the model
The model keeps the data given by the user as named parameters or variables, not only in formulas

evals.name: bread-too-low
evals.prompt: The climate impact of my bread in this lcaac model looks too low to me. Can you find out why and fix it?
evals.expected_output: Both silent errors are fixed: the heat input selects the gas oven with all its labels (energy and country), and the CO2 emission gives the compartment air. The bread then emits 0.725 kg CO2-eq per kg (0.4 flour, 0.125 heat, 0.2 CO2), and no unresolved flow remains.

assertions.text: One kg of bread emits 0.725 kg CO2-eq
No unresolved flow remains in the results of bread
The tests of the model pass
The explanation names both causes: the incomplete match of the oven's labels, and the missing compartment of the CO2 emission

evals.name: server-fleet
evals.prompt: I have an inventory of servers in data/servers.csv: id, power (W), hours of use per year, and embodied GWP per year (kg CO2-eq). Write an lcaac model of the yearly GWP of the fleet: the embodied impacts plus the electricity they consume, at 0.06 kg CO2-eq per kWh. I want to see the contribution of each server. The main process should be called fleet.
evals.expected_output: A model reading data/servers.csv as a data source, with one process per server (for_each over the rows, passing the id), and a process fleet whose GWP is 724.2 kg CO2-eq per year (330 embodied, 394.2 from 6570 kWh of electricity). lcaac trace fleet shows a row per server.

assertions.text: The fleet emits 724.2 kg CO2-eq per year
The climate impact is in the prelude's unit kg_CO2_Eq, not in a unit declared by the model
The trace of fleet shows each server
The model reads the inventory from data/servers.csv, rather than copying its values

evals.name: pool-lookup
evals.prompt: In my lcaac model, pool b has a single server, web-1, which draws 600 W all year and has 200 kg CO2-eq of embodied impacts per year. The GWP of pool b looks too low to me, though. Can you find the problem and fix it?
evals.expected_output: The lookup of a server by id alone takes the first row with that id, web-1 of pool a: the fix filters on the pool too (match (id = id, pool = pool), passing the pool), or on a unique key. Pool b then emits 462.8 kg CO2-eq per year (5256 kWh at 0.05, plus 200), and pool a is unchanged at 462.8.

assertions.text: Pool b emits 462.8 kg CO2-eq per year
Pool a still emits 462.8 kg CO2-eq per year
The tests of the model pass
The explanation names the cause: a lookup by id alone takes the first of several matching rows

evals.name: study-period
evals.prompt: My lcaac model assesses a web service over one year: 8760 hours, hard-coded. Make the period a global parameter named period, so that I can assess the service over a month (720 hours) without editing the model.
evals.expected_output: A global parameter period (params block at the top level), defaulting to 8760 hour and used by the service for both inputs. lcaac assess service gives 219 kg CO2-eq, and with -G period="720 hour" 18 kg CO2-eq.

assertions.text: Over a year (the default), the service emits 219 kg CO2-eq
Over a month, set with -G period, the service emits 18 kg CO2-eq
The answer tells how to assess another period (lcaac assess service -G period=...)

evals.name: heat-pump
evals.prompt: Model with lcaac the yearly climate impact of a 3 kW heat pump running 2000 hours a year, on electricity at 0.06 kg CO2-eq per kWh. It also leaks 0.5 kg of R410A refrigerant to the air every year (GWP 2088 kg CO2-eq per kg). Call the main process heat_pump.
evals.expected_output: A model with a process heat_pump: 6000 kWh of electricity (360 kg CO2-eq) and the leak (1044 kg CO2-eq), 1404 kg CO2-eq a year, in the prelude's kg_CO2_Eq. kW declared as a unit (the prelude has W only), the leak characterized (a substance with its compartment, or an impact), no unresolved flow.

assertions.text: The heat pump emits 1404 kg CO2-eq per year
The climate impact is in the prelude's unit kg_CO2_Eq, not in a unit declared by the model
No unresolved product or substance is left (the electricity and the refrigerant are characterized)
The power and the leak are parameters of the model
